name: Codebase Mapping for Brownfield Projects
description: Add 'fade map' command that analyzes an existing codebase and generates context for FADE.md. Critical for brownfield projects where developers are adding FADE to an existing repo. Inspired by GSD's /gsd:map-codebase which spawns agents to analyze stack, architecture, conventions, and concerns before planning.

userStories.title: Basic codebase analysis
userStories.description: As a developer adding FADE to an existing project, I want to run 'fade map' to get an automated analysis of my codebase structure
acceptanceCriteria: fade map command exists and is documented in help
Detects primary language(s) by file extension counts
Detects framework (React, Express, Django, etc.) from package.json/requirements.txt/etc
Identifies entry points (main.py, index.js, app.ts, etc.)
Lists top-level directory structure with brief descriptions
Output is formatted for easy copy-paste into FADE.md

userStories.title: Architecture pattern detection
userStories.description: As a developer, I want fade map to identify common architectural patterns so I understand how the codebase is organized
acceptanceCriteria: Detects MVC/MVVM patterns from directory names (models/, views/, controllers/)
Detects API structure (routes/, api/, endpoints/)
Detects test organization (tests/, __tests__/, spec/)
Detects config patterns (config/, .env files, settings/)
Reports detected patterns with confidence level (certain/likely/possible)

userStories.title: Dependency analysis
userStories.description: As a developer, I want fade map to summarize my project's dependencies so FADE.md captures the tech stack
acceptanceCriteria: Reads package.json (npm), requirements.txt/pyproject.toml (Python), Cargo.toml (Rust), go.mod (Go)
Categorizes dependencies: framework, database, testing, utilities
Highlights major dependencies (React, Express, Django, FastAPI, etc.)
Notes dev vs production dependencies where applicable
Output suitable for Tech Stack section of FADE.md

userStories.title: Generate FADE.md draft
userStories.description: As a developer, I want fade map to optionally generate a draft FADE.md pre-populated with discovered context
acceptanceCriteria: fade map --init generates FADE.md if it doesn't exist
Populates Tech Stack section from dependency analysis
Populates Project Overview with detected framework/language
Populates Architecture References with detected patterns
Marks all generated content with <!-- AUTO-GENERATED --> comments
Warns user to review and customize auto-generated content
Does not overwrite existing FADE.md (use --force to override)

userStories.title: Identify potential fragile areas
userStories.description: As a developer, I want fade map to flag potential problem areas so I can populate the Fragile Areas section
acceptanceCriteria: Flags files over 500 lines as potentially complex
Flags directories with many files (>20) as potentially tangled
Flags files with 'legacy', 'old', 'deprecated' in name/path
Flags files with many TODO/FIXME/HACK comments
Output formatted for Fragile Areas table in FADE.md

userStories.title: Respect gitignore
userStories.description: As a developer, I want fade map to respect .gitignore so it doesn't analyze node_modules, venv, build artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Reads .gitignore if present
Excludes gitignored paths from analysis
Also excludes common defaults: node_modules/, venv/, .git/, dist/, build/
Reports count of excluded paths for transparency

technicalNotes.approach: Use shell commands (find, wc, grep) for analysis rather than spawning Claude agents. Keep it fast and deterministic.
technicalNotes.outputFormat: Markdown sections ready for copy-paste or direct insertion into FADE.md
technicalNotes.gsdComparison: GSD uses parallel agents for mapping. FADE takes simpler approach with shell analysis - faster, no API costs, deterministic results.
technicalNotes.futureEnhancement: Could add --deep flag that uses Claude to analyze code semantics, but start with fast shell-based analysis
